title: Sample Preparation for Lipidomics in Metabolomics
author: Oliver Fiehn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ytpfwmn

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Solvents
steps.instruction: Prepare the cooling bath and extraction solvents for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Switch on bath to pre-cool at –20°C (±2°C validity temperature range).
Purge both MeOH and MTBE for 5 min with nitrogen.
Store solvents in the –20°C freezer to pre-chill.

steps.title: Homogenize Plasma Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the plasma samples for extraction.

substeps.instruction: Thaw plasma on ice.
Gently rotate or invert the blood samples for about 10s to obtain a homogenized sample.

steps.title: Perform Lipid Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract lipids from the plasma using a methanol and MTBE solvent system.

substeps.instruction: Take 60 µL of sample and add 220 µL cold MeOH.
Add 5 µL of QC mix as internal standard.
Vortex each sample for 10s, keeping the remaining samples on ice.
Add 750 µL MTBE.
Vortex for 10s.
Shake for 6min at 4°C.
Add 187.5 µL distilled water.
Vortex for 20s.
Centrifuge for 2 min @ 14000 rcf.

steps.title: Collect and Dry Supernatant
steps.instruction: Isolate the lipid-containing layer and remove solvents.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant and split into two aliquots of 300 µL.
Store one 300 µL aliquot at –20°C for backup.
Dry the remaining sample to complete dryness in the speed vacuum concentration system.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for Analysis
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried lipids and transfer to vials for LC-MS.

substeps.instruction: Re-suspend dry samples in 70 µL MeOH containing CUDA (10 µM), degassed using the nitrogen purge method.
Transfer 30 µL to two separate amber glass vials with micro-inserts.
Cap vials with Agilent blue top.
Use independent vials for positive and negative mode acquisitions.

steps.title: Implement Quality Assurance
steps.instruction: Include controls for each sequence of sample extractions.

substeps.instruction: Perform one blank negative control extraction (all materials and plastic ware, no biological sample).
Use one commercial plasma/serum pool sample per 10 authentic subject samples as control.
If no commercial sample is available, prepare a large pool by aliquoting 100 ul per 1 ml plasma sample, then use 1 pool extract per 10 authentic subject samples.
Prepare at least six NIST plasma extracts in the same manner as positive controls.
